common_name: Sweet Jade Kabocha Squash (AAS-Winning Personal-Size Kabocha)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost once soil has warmed, or start indoors a couple weeks early; Sweet Jade grows on a more restrained vine than standard kabocha types and rewards a bit less garden space.

directions: Direct sow in warm, fertile soil in full sun after frost danger has passed, giving the semi-compact vine room to ramble. Sweet Jade is an AAS-winning kabocha bred by Johnny's Selected Seeds for a personal-serving size, yielding round, 1 to 2 pound fruit with a jade-green, lightly speckled rind that encloses deep orange, richly sweet flesh often compared to a blend of pumpkin, sweet potato, and roasted chestnut. Let fruit fully harden on the vine before cutting, then cure in a warm spot for a week or two to concentrate sugars before moving to cool storage. Its smaller fruit size makes it easy to portion a whole squash per person for roasting or stuffing.
sources: All-America Selections — Sweet Jade Kabocha winner announcement

common_name: San Joaquin Jalapeño Pepper (AAS-Winning Compact High-Yield Jalapeño)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; San Joaquin forms a compact, upright bush around 30 inches tall that suits a large container as easily as an open bed.

directions: Start seed indoors at warm soil temperature and transplant after all frost danger has passed into full sun. San Joaquin is an AAS-winning jalapeño bred for a tidy, determinate bush habit that concentrates its heavy fruit set into a shorter window, often producing dozens of thick-walled, crack-resistant, roughly 4-inch pods per plant. Peppers hold mild jalapeño heat and can be picked green for classic use or left to ripen to red for a sweeter, still-mild flavor. The sturdy, compact plant needs little staking and performs well in containers, making it a good choice for smaller gardens wanting a big jalapeño harvest for pickling and stuffing.
sources: All-America Selections — Pepper jalapeno San Joaquin F1 winner announcement
Bejo Seeds variety notes

common_name: Wildcat Cayenne Pepper (AAS-Winning Extra-Large Straight Cayenne)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; Wildcat is a compact, even-growing cayenne plant that carries an unusually heavy load of long, straight fruit.

directions: Start seed indoors and transplant into full sun after frost danger has passed. Wildcat is an AAS regional winner selected for extra-large cayenne pods, roughly 8 inches long and straighter than typical cayenne fruit, with thicker, fleshier walls than older varieties. Heat is notably mild for a cayenne, in the 500-1500 Scoville range, giving a smoky, peppery sweetness that works well fresh, dried, or ground. The strong, compact, evenly branching plant sets fruit heavily and holds up well through the growing season with routine picking to encourage continued production.
sources: All-America Selections — Pepper cayenne Wildcat F1 winner announcement
Totally Tomatoes variety notes

common_name: Purple Magic Broccoli (AAS-Winning Purple-Headed, Purple-Stemmed Broccoli)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost for a spring crop, or in midsummer for a fall crop; heat- and stress-tolerant, Purple Magic performs across a wider range of regions and seasons than most broccoli.

directions: Start transplants and set out into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in early spring or midsummer. Purple Magic is an AAS-winning broccoli notable for carrying purple color not just in the head but through the stems and leaves as well, a first among broccoli breeding, driven by a high anthocyanin content that also gives the roughly 1-pound domed heads a sweeter taste than green broccoli. The uniform, well-domed crowns hold their vivid color well after harvest and even through light cooking. Harvest the central head while buds are still tight, then keep picking side shoots as they form to extend the season; the plant tolerates heat stress better than many broccoli varieties, easing timing in warmer regions.
sources: All-America Selections — Broccoli Purple Magic F1 winner announcement
Johnny's Selected Seeds variety notes

common_name: Red Impact Sweet Pepper (AAS-Winning Lamuyo-Type Bull's Horn Pepper)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; Red Impact is a Lamuyo-type sweet pepper, an elongated, blocky Mediterranean type that is notoriously fussy in other varieties but bred here for easier, more reliable garden performance.

directions: Start seed indoors at warm soil temperature and transplant into full sun once frost danger has passed. Red Impact is an AAS-winning Lamuyo-type sweet pepper bearing large, roughly 7-inch tapered fruit that ripens from green to deep red, with unusually thick, sweet walls even before the fruit fully colors. Plants grow upright and tidy with a strong disease-resistance package, setting a heavy load of uniform fruit that finishes reliably. Harvest green for a milder, crisper pepper or let fruit ripen fully to red for the sweetest flavor and best eating quality; consistent watering during fruit set helps prevent thin walls and blossom-end rot.
sources: All-America Selections — Pepper Red Impact F1 winner announcement
Park Seed variety notes

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant 2-4 weeks before last frost, and again in late summer for a fall crop; Konstance holds in the garden longer than older purple kohlrabi without becoming pithy or cracking.

directions: Direct sow, or start transplants and set out 2-4 weeks before last frost, into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Konstance is an AAS-winning purple kohlrabi bred from the same breeding line as Kolibri, improved with smoother skin, more upright foliage, and better resistance to fusarium, and it holds a vivid purple color that extends into the leaf stems. The crisp, sweet, peppery bulb stays crack-resistant and tender over a longer harvest window than older varieties, so a planting does not have to be picked all at once. Harvest bulbs at 2-3 inches for the most tender texture, and use young leaves as a cooked or raw green in addition to the bulb itself.
sources: All-America Selections — Kohlrabi Konstance F1 winner announcement
Territorial Seed variety notes

common_name: Green Lightning Pattypan Squash (AAS-Winning Striped Scallop Summer Squash)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; Green Lightning is an early, compact bush pattypan suited to smaller gardens, with fruit ready to pick quickly after flowering.

directions: Direct sow seed after the danger of frost has passed into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Green Lightning is an AAS-winning pattypan summer squash with a compact bush habit and glossy, scalloped fruit striped in dark green over a lighter green background, giving it a more vivid, eye-catching look than typical solid-colored pattypans. A small seed cavity keeps more of the fruit as tender, edible flesh compared to older scallop types. Harvest young, at about 3-5 inches across, for the best texture and flavor, and pick every day or two once plants start producing to keep the vigorous bush setting new fruit.
sources: All-America Selections — Squash Green Lightning F1 winner announcement
Fedco Seeds variety notes

common_name: Murasaki Fioretto Cauliflower (AAS-Winning Purple Long-Stem Sprouting Cauliflower)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost for a spring crop, or in midsummer for a fall crop; Murasaki (Japanese for 'purple') is part of the long-stemmed Fioretto series rather than a traditional single-head cauliflower.

directions: Start transplants and set out into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Murasaki Fioretto is an AAS-winning stick-type cauliflower that first forms a compact purple head, then elongates into loose, bunchable, tender-stemmed florets that can be harvested at 3-4 inches for bagging or left to reach 8 inches for bunching, similar in habit to broccolini. Its vivid violet-purple color is heat tolerant and stays vibrant through cooking, shifting to fuchsia when pickled and to golden brown when roasted or sautéed. The mild, sweet flavor and tender stems need no peeling, and the compact plant holds in the field well past typical cauliflower harvest windows without declining in quality.
sources: All-America Selections — Cauliflower Murasaki Fioretto 70 F1 winner announcement
Johnny's Selected Seeds variety notes

common_name: Tonatico Cherry Tomato (AAS-Winning High-Yield Round Cherry Tomato)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; Tonatico is a tall, upright indeterminate cherry tomato that benefits from staking or caging to support its long fruit trusses.

directions: Start seed indoors and transplant into full sun after the last frost, staking or caging the tall indeterminate vine well before it needs the support. Tonatico is an AAS regional winner producing round, bright red, roughly 1.5-inch cherry fruit with a notably high sugar content and juicy, sweet flavor, carried on long, easy-to-harvest trusses that can number up to 200 fruits per plant over the season. Fruit resists cracking and the plant shows good disease resistance, so the uniform clusters hold up well through variable watering and weather. Pick trusses as fruit fully colors for the sweetest eating, and maintain consistent moisture to keep the high yields coming.
sources: All-America Selections — Tomato Tonatico F1 winner announcement

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant in early spring, and again in late summer for a fall crop; kale is also a strong candidate for fall planting since cool weather and light frost sweeten the leaves.

directions: Direct sow or start transplants in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Rubybor is an AAS-winning curly kale that scored a Gold Medal in both ornamental and vegetable trials, an unusual double distinction, thanks to finely frilled leaves with deep purple stems and veining that hold their color even through summer heat. The leaves stay tender and mild enough for raw salads while remaining sturdy enough for cooking, and the compact, bushy plant produces roughly twice the yield of older red kale varieties. Harvest outer leaves from the bottom up as needed, and expect improved sweetness in leaves picked after a light frost.
sources: All-America Selections — Kale Rubybor F1 winner announcement
Johnny's Selected Seeds variety notes

common_name: Butter Lamp Squash (AAS-Winning Mini Butternut-Type Winter Squash)

planting.note: Direct sow after all danger of frost has passed and soil has warmed; Butter Lamp grows on shorter vines than standard butternut, needing less garden space, and can also be trained up a trellis.

directions: Direct sow into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the soil has warmed. Butter Lamp is an AAS-winning butternut-type squash bred for a mini, pumpkin-shaped fruit weighing about 1 to 2 pounds, with rich yellow, smooth, sweet and nutty flesh and strong resistance to powdery mildew, heat, and insect pressure. The short-vined plant needs notably less garden space than traditional butternut squash and can be grown as a trellised hanging fruit or left to sprawl on the ground. Harvest once the rind hardens fully and resists a fingernail scratch; fruit stores exceptionally well into winter when cured in a warm, dry spot for a week or two first.
sources: All-America Selections — Squash winter Butter Lamp F1 winner announcement
Known-You Seed variety notes

common_name: BadaBing! Tomato (AAS-Winning Crack-Resistant Large Cherry Tomato)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; BadaBing! is indeterminate but stays fairly compact at around 40 inches tall, so it still benefits from a stake or cage.

directions: Start seed indoors and transplant into full sun after the last frost, staking or caging the vine to support fruit clusters. BadaBing! is an AAS-winning large cherry, nearly cocktail-sized tomato, bearing juicy, bright red, roughly 1.5 to 2 inch fruit with excellent flavor and strong resistance to cracking even after rain. It carries notable resistance to septoria leaf spot, early blight, and late blight, which helps keep foliage healthier through a humid season. Despite an indeterminate growth habit, the plant stays relatively compact, making it a good fit for large containers as well as garden beds; pick fruit as it fully colors for the best flavor and to keep the vigorous plant setting more.
sources: All-America Selections — Tomato BadaBing! F1 winner announcement
Holmes Seed Company variety notes

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost at warm soil temperature; Treviso's tight, highly branched habit makes it well suited to large containers as well as garden beds.

directions: Start seeds indoors at warm soil temperature and transplant after the last frost into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Treviso is an AAS-winning basil with a compact, dense, highly branched habit and leaves carrying a subtle anise note alongside classic basil sweetness. It is notably slow to bolt and holds tender, non-bitter leaf quality later into the season than many culinary basils, with good heat tolerance and foliage that resists browning or oxidizing after cutting. Pinch growing tips regularly and remove flower spikes as they form to keep the plant bushy and productive, harvesting leaves anytime once established for fresh use or pesto.
sources: All-America Selections — Basil Treviso winner announcement
